Kubernetes.Name: Kubernetes
Kubernetes.NotInstalled: kubectl is not installed. Install kubectl (or set FM_KUBECTL to the kubectl program, or name it in the plugin's settings), then open this again.
Kubernetes.NoSuchContext: No such context in the kubeconfig: {0}
Kubernetes.NoAnswer: The cluster of the context {0} does not answer: check the network (a VPN?) and that the cluster runs, then try again.
Kubernetes.LoginRefused: The cluster did not accept the login of the context {0}: log in again (renew the credentials of the kubeconfig), then try again.
Kubernetes.ContainerStopped: The container is not running in the pod {0}: its files can be reached only while it runs (the pod's logs may tell why).
Kubernetes.Forbidden: The cluster refused it: the account of the context {0} has no right to do this. Ask the cluster's administrator for a role that allows it.
Kubernetes.NoShell: The container has no shell (sh), so its files cannot be listed.
Kubernetes.BadKubeconfig: kubectl gave a kubeconfig it could not read itself: check the kubeconfig file.
Kubernetes.NoContexts: The kubeconfig has no contexts: add a cluster with its own tool (for example az aks get-credentials, aws eks update-kubeconfig, gcloud container clusters get-credentials, kind or minikube), then open this again.
Kubernetes.MoveBetween: Moving between containers is done by copying.
Kubernetes.MadeWithKubectl: Namespaces, pods and containers are made and removed with kubectl itself.
Kubernetes.NoLogLines: The pod has written no log lines.
Kubernetes.DeletePodQuestion: Delete the pod {0}? A pod of a deployment (or of another controller) is made again by it.
Kubernetes.DeletePodsQuestion: Delete {0} pods? Pods of a deployment (or of another controller) are made again by it.
Kubernetes.RestartQuestion: Restart the deployment {0}? Its pods are replaced one by one.
Kubernetes.KubectlProgramHelp: Empty: FM_KUBECTL, then kubectl on the PATH and in the usual folders.
Kubernetes.KubeconfigHelp: Empty: the one kubectl reads itself (the KUBECONFIG environment variable, else .kube/config in the home folder).
Kubernetes.LogLinesHelp: How many of a pod's last log lines Pod logs shows.
